Time horizon.d: In METR's research, the length of task (measured by how long skilled humans take) that an AI agent completes successfully about half the time.

Mechanistic interpretability.d: Research that tries to work out the actual internal mechanisms (features and circuits) by which a neural network produces its outputs.

World model.d: A learned model of how an environment behaves, letting a system predict what will happen next if it takes an action.

Vision-language-action model.d: A robot-control model built on a pre-trained vision-language model, which takes in images and instructions and outputs robot actions.

Scalable oversight.d: Methods that let humans supervise AI systems reliably even on tasks where the AI is more capable than the supervisor, often by using AI to help check AI.

Chain-of-thought monitoring.d: Reading or automatically scanning a model's written reasoning to catch signs of mistakes or intended misbehaviour before it acts.

Continual learning.d: A model learning new things after deployment without forgetting what it already knows. Largely unsolved for large language models, whose weights are frozen after training.

Capstone project.d: A substantial final project that combines many skills from a course into one working result, assessed against a rubric.

Marking guide.d: A document that tells an assessor what a good answer contains and how many marks each part earns, so different markers grade consistently.

Portfolio.d: A collection of finished work (projects, write-ups, code, reports) that shows what you can do, used for reviews and job applications.
